proof.text: Relabel the rings as $A\to B\to C$. The differential-presheaf lemma supplies the small pair site $\mathcal E$, its three $C$-module presheaves and the canonical short exact sequence $0\to M_1\xrightarrow a M_2\xrightarrow b M_3\to0$. Apply the exact bar functor to obtain the degreewise short exact sequence $0\to X_1\xrightarrow{K(a)}X_2\xrightarrow{K(b)}X_3\to0$, where $X_i=K_{\mathcal E}(M_i)$. Its short-exact-complex boundary $\delta:X_3\to X_1[1]$ gives a distinguished triangle, natural for morphisms of these sequences.

source.place: Tags 08QU (lemma-triangle-ses) and 08QX (proposition-triangle); sites-cohomology Tag 08PG; derived Tag 0152.

proof.text: The term-identification lemma gives the specified isomorphisms $\alpha_1:X_1\simeq L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C$, $\alpha_2:X_2\simeq L_{C/A}$, $\alpha_3:X_3\simeq L_{C/B}$, including the free-value verification needed for the first derived tensor. The arrow-comparison lemma gives $\alpha_2K(a)=f\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_3K(b)=g\alpha_2$, where $f,g$ are the standard functoriality arrows. By (TR1), transport the distinguished triangle along these three isomorphisms, setting $\partial=\alpha_1[1]\delta\alpha_3^{-1}$. Its first two arrows are therefore exactly $f,g$.

source.place: Tags 08QX (proposition-triangle), term identifications, and 08QL (section-functoriality), comparison of arrows.

proof.text:
For a diagram of triples let $R=\operatorname{Res}_{C'/C}$. The diagram-compatibility lemma gives a morphism $T_i:X_i\to RX_i'$ of short exact bar sequences and $(R\alpha_i')T_i=f_i\alpha_i$. The bar lemma's semilinear connecting-map compatibility identifies the boundary of the restricted target sequence with $R\delta'$, using the canonical shift identification. Short-exact-complex boundary naturality gives $T_1[1]\delta=(R\delta')T_3$. Thus
$$f_1[1]\partial=(R\alpha_1')[1]T_1[1]\delta\alpha_3^{-1}=(R\alpha_1')[1](R\delta')T_3\alpha_3^{-1}=(R\partial')f_3.$$
All these maps lie in $D(C)$. The other two squares follow from the morphism of sequences and step 2. Identity and composition follow from the diagram lemma. Hence the transported distinguished triangle is canonical and natural, including its boundary, for arbitrary ring diagrams. Relabel $B,C$ back to $P,B$.

title: Transitivity triangle for ring cotangent complexes
statement: Let $A\to P\to B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. With the standard cotangent complexes of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], there is a canonical distinguished triangle $L_{P/A}\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}B\to L_{B/A}\to L_{B/P}\to(L_{P/A}\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}B)[1]$ in $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The first two arrows are the standard functoriality arrows for the ring maps. The triangle is natural under commutative diagrams of triples of ring maps.
